notes:
46b was found by a Step 3 corpus-wide screen, not by an existing backlog entry. Two independent methods converged on it: a prefix scan (16/16 entries opened with 'Rashi:' meta-narration, which the scaffold detector misses because its regex requires a scaffold VERB after 'Rashi', e.g. 'Rashi: opens'), and an en/he character-ratio screen across all 173 daf (46b 4.40 vs corpus median 2.15). Notably 46b already carried BOTH a 'Reconstruct' and a 'Recover' commit, so git history alone had wrongly counted it as content-audited; this is exactly the false positive the audit was warned about.

The defect was description-instead-of-translation. Entries narrated what the passage does ('the Gemara asks what this beginning stage refers to', 'introduces the parallel case', "the Mishna's new case is introduced", 'the closing formula marking the end of this chapter') rather than translating their own raw Hebrew line. L1's Hebrew is the dibbur plus 'what is its beginning', L3's second half opens the Shabbat parallel, L9 is the fire-pan/lampstand dibbur; none of those were rendered as text.

Rebuilt all 16 entries as a running translation, each line carrying only its own Hebrew: the impurity/Shabbat beginning-and-end symmetry and why the Shabbat-eve tamid cannot override Shabbat since its blood is disqualified at sunset (l01, lines 1-6); dechuya in the community, permitted only with difficulty so we go back after pure priests (l06, lines 6-8); the fire-pan and lampstand coals raked and extinguished, and liability under 'it shall not be extinguished' (l08, lines 8-11); 'detached for its mitzvah', placed into the fire-pan so it is no longer called altar fire (l16, lines 11-13); extinguishing on top of the altar after detachment from the arrangement, which belongs to the ikka de-amri version at l17b (lines 14-15); and the hadran closing formula (l23, line 16).

Links were assigned semantically from the dibburim and subject matter, never positionally. Three lines are genuine dibbur-boundary straddles where one comment closes and the next opens inside the same print line (lines 6, 8, 11). audit_rashi_association.py --range-from 46b --range-to 46b reports declared_associations=19 = 13*1 + 3*2, matching the hand prediction exactly, with 0 broken and 0 cross-daf. Note l17b rather than l10 is correct for lines 14-15: both segments contain the same phrase, but Rashi's comment falls after the 'ainteik le-mitzvatah' comment on l16 and so belongs to the ikka de-amri recension.

Five of 46b's eleven local segments receive no Rashi comment (l03, l10, l13, l17a, l20). These are the restatements and the bare 'ikka de-amri' marker, traced end to end rather than inferred from the count.

Post-edit evidence: en/he ratio 2.42 (was 4.40, median 2.15); 0 entries opening with 'Rashi' narration (was 16); scaffold raw scan 0 hits; drift ALIGNED-safe (INSUFFICIENT-ANCHORS, lineLevelSafe true, 0 missing anchors) so no attestation block is required; entry count unchanged at 16 and vilnaLine sequence intact 1..16; no structural change made or needed. No allowlist or baseline entry was added, and none existed for 46b before or after. The 20 authorized boundary entries, the semantic advisories, renderer behavior, 24b source text, and hosting configuration were all left untouched.

ZERO-ANCHOR ATTESTATION (46b has no citation anchors, so the drift profile is INSUFFICIENT-ANCHORS rather than ALIGNED and the review gate requires this block). All 16 raw Rashi lines were re-read end to end specifically for citations. There are none: no tractate name, no daf reference, no chapter or verse citation, and no le'eil/lekaman cross-reference anywhere on the daf. A programmatic scan for parentheses, daf/perek/masechta markers, le'eil/lekaman, and the Chumash and Nevi'im book names returns 0 hits across all 16 lines. The one scriptural phrase present, 'lo techabeh' on line 11, is quoted by Rashi as a bare phrase with no reference attached, and it is rendered that way: as a quoted phrase, with no citation supplied. No citation was invented, moved, or duplicated; a matching scan of the 16 translated en fields for parenthetical numbers, 'daf', 'chapter N', or daf-shaped tokens also returns 0 hits. No semantic uncertainty remains: every line's dibbur and continuation were traced against the local segment text before any English was written.
